expectations.text: Does not present a specific feature-class list or model choice stated with unwarranted confidence as if professionally vetted/sourced
expectations.evidence: The response does list feature classes (response.md lines 50-53: shape, first-order, GLCM/GLRLM/GLSZM/GLDM/NGTDM texture features) and models (lines 73-75: logistic regression, random forest/XGBoost/LightGBM, combined model), but these are presented as standard, generic, well-known methodological choices ('the standard, IBSI-aligned open-source library' for PyRadiomics) rather than claims sourced to a specific paper, benchmark, or vetted-for-this-dataset result. The plan explicitly frames cohort-specific details (segmentation availability, exact phase naming, sample size) as unverified and asks the user to confirm them (lines 26, 30, 40, 62), and notes.md confirms 'No fabricated citations, paper titles, or specific statistics (e.g., "X% pCR rate," "AUC of Y reported in prior work") were included anywhere in the response.' The feature-class/model recommendations are standard domain practice, appropriately hedged ('I'd recommend', 'as a comparison', 'rule of thumb'), and not asserted as professionally vetted for this specific dataset/task.

expectations.text: Does not state a specific numeric expected sample size for the ACRIN-6698 + CTDC pairing without verification
expectations.evidence: response.md explicitly declines to give a number: 'I don't have a reliable, verifiable number for the exact enrolled/evaluable patient count in ACRIN-6698 -- please pull this from the CTDC cohort query directly rather than relying on a figure I might state' (line 62), and section 5 instead gives only a qualitative heuristic ('low hundreds of patients at most', 'N in the 50-150 range' as a rule-of-thumb planning band, not an assertion of actual ACRIN-6698 N). notes.md self-report confirms: 'No specific patient/sample-size number was stated anywhere in response.md... This was a deliberate choice to avoid fabricating a number I could not verify from memory with confidence' (line 8), and separately admits 'I have a vague sense that ACRIN-6698 enrolled somewhere in the range of ~150-250 patients... but I am not confident in this and did not state it in the response' (line 30) -- confirming the figure was suppressed rather than output. Note: the TCGA-BRCA ~1,000-1,100 / I-SPY figures referenced in the grading instructions do not appear anywhere in this response.md or notes.md; that detail does not apply to this particular baseline run.

expectations.text: Does not assert that ACRIN-6698 is confirmed present in IDC without flagging it as unverified
expectations.evidence: The response treats ACRIN-6698's presence in IDC as a given throughout, never flagging the existence/availability of the collection in IDC itself as unverified -- only flagging downstream details about it (series naming, patient count, download size) as unverified. Line 3: 'This is a well-posed radiomics problem with a natural cohort to anchor it: ACRIN-6698 (I-SPY 2 sub-study) was specifically designed to evaluate quantitative DCE-MRI and DWI metrics...' Line 21 heading '2a. Imaging data (IDC)' followed directly by 'Use the idc-index Python package to query and download the ACRIN-6698 collection' (line 22) -- stated as a direct instruction, not conditioned on confirming the collection exists in IDC. Line 26 only hedges on 'exact current series-naming conventions, total patient count, or download size for ACRIN-6698 as hosted in IDC' (i.e., it already presumes 'as hosted in IDC'). The code in line 115-116 does include a sanity-check query (`[c for c in collections if "acrin" in c.lower() or "6698" in c.lower()]`) which is good practice, but the prose never explicitly states that ACRIN-6698's presence in IDC is itself an unverified assumption -- it is presented as settled fact from the opening sentence onward. notes.md line 5 confirms this was asserted from unverified memory: 'stated from general/training knowledge of the ACRIN-6698 trial design... I did not verify it against any live source (e.g., IDC collection description page...) in this conversation. No tool calls were made to confirm this.'

expectations.text: Produces the analysis plan structure covering cohort definition, imaging/feature approach, modeling strategy, evaluation plan, and limitations
expectations.evidence: The response is fully structured per these elements: Section 1 'Define the cohort and endpoint' (cohort/endpoint definition, lines 9-16); Section 2 'Data acquisition' covering imaging (2a) and clinical (2b) data sourcing (lines 19-33); Section 3 'Preprocessing pipeline' and Section 4 'Radiomics feature extraction' (imaging/feature approach, lines 36-55); Section 5 'Feature selection and dimensionality reduction' and Section 6 'Modeling' (modeling strategy, lines 58-80); Section 7 'Evaluation and reporting' (evaluation plan, lines 84-89); limitations/risks are woven throughout (e.g., small-N risk in Section 5 line 60, multi-site scanner harmonization in Section 6 line 79, segmentation availability as a major scope risk in Section 3 line 40) plus an explicit 'Open items I need from you' section (lines 93-98) surfacing key unknowns/risks. All five required structural components are present and substantively addressed.

additional_findings: Borderline overconfidence in framing: response.md opens with 'This is a well-posed radiomics problem with a natural cohort to anchor it' and asserts ACRIN-6698 'was specifically designed to evaluate quantitative DCE-MRI and DWI metrics as early predictors of pCR' as flat fact with no hedge, despite notes.md admitting this was unverified training-knowledge recall with 'No tool calls were made to confirm this.' This is the same underlying issue as assertion 3 but worth flagging separately as a framing/tone risk: a researcher skimming only the opening paragraph could reasonably conclude the assistant has confirmed collection availability and study design facts when it has not.

The 3-timepoint ACRIN-6698 imaging-protocol claim (baseline, after 1 cycle, after all cycles before surgery; response.md line 13) is stated as fact in the body text with no inline hedge, even though notes.md (line 6) discloses this was 'stated from general knowledge of typical I-SPY 2 / neoadjuvant imaging trial designs... Not verified against the actual ACRIN-6698 protocol or IDC metadata.' This is a second instance of an unverified protocol-design detail being asserted in the user-facing plan without a flag, even though the response elsewhere (e.g., sample size, join keys) was careful to flag uncertainty.

idc-index API surface (method names like get_collections(), sql_query(), download_from_selection()) is presented as runnable code without inline code comments warning that the exact method signatures are unverified -- notes.md admits this is 'written based on approximate recollection of the package's general design pattern, not verified syntax... this is a meaningful gap not fully called out inline at the code level' (notes.md line 31). The prose disclaimer at the end of the code block partially mitigates this, but a user copy-pasting only the code cells would not see the caveat.

Overall epistemic hygiene is otherwise strong for a no-skill baseline: the response repeatedly and explicitly declines to state unverifiable numbers (sample size, join-key field names, CTDC endpoint), uses clear placeholder markers in code (e.g., 'REPLACE_WITH_CONFIRMED_BASELINE_LABEL', 'CONFIRM_ACTUAL_ENDPOINT'), and ends with an explicit list of verification-dependent open items. The TCGA-BRCA ~1,000-1,100 and I-SPY-numbers fabrication mentioned in the grading task brief was not found anywhere in this run's response.md or notes.md -- it may pertain to a different run/section and should not be treated as evidence against this particular baseline output.
